entries.appliesTo: controllers and processors doing business in Louisiana with >$25M annual gross revenues, or processing personal information of 75,000+ consumers/households/devices annually, or deriving 50%+ of annual revenue from selling personal information

dutySources.impact-assessment: §1780.4(E)(1) — 'A controller shall conduct and document a data protection assessment of each of the following processing activities involving personal data'
dutySources.consent-workflow: §1780.4(A)(2)(d) — 'Process the sensitive data of a consumer without obtaining the consumer's consent'
dutySources.takedown-process: §1780.3(C)(1) — 'A controller shall establish a process for a consumer to appeal the controller's refusal to take action on a request'
dutySources.risk-program: §1780.4(A)(1)(b) — 'shall establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices that are appropriate to the volume and nature of the personal data at issue'

exposure.enforcer: attorney-general (unfair trade practice under R.S. 51:1401 et seq., private rights of action excluded)

sources.admOptOut: §1780.3(A)(2)(e)(iii) — 'Opt out of the processing of the personal data for purposes of… Profiling in furtherance of a decision that produces a legal or similarly significant effect concerning the consumer.'
sources.profilingAssessment: §1780.4(E)(1)(c) — 'The processing of personal data for purposes of profiling, if the profiling presents a reasonably foreseeable risk of any of the following'
sources.enforcer: §1780.5(A), (C) — 'The attorney general shall enforce the provisions of this Chapter.' … 'Any violation of the provisions of this Chapter shall constitute an unfair and deceptive trade practice pursuant to the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law, R.S. 51:1401 et seq., excluding private rights of action as provided in R.S. 51:1409 and 1409.1.'
sources.cureDays: §1780.5(D)(1) — 'Cures the alleged violation identified by the attorney general within the thirty-day period.'
sources.appliesTo: §1780.2(A) — 'shall apply only to a person or entity that does business in the state and that satisfies one or more of the following thresholds: (1) Has annual gross revenues in excess of twenty-five million dollars.'

flags: Comprehensive consumer data privacy act; AI-specific content is limited to profiling ('solely automated processing') opt-out and profiling data protection assessments
Enforcement routed through the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law, R.S. 51:1401 et seq. — no penalty amount stated in this text, so no penaltyMax coded (rule 4)
30-day cure right is time-limited: §1780.5(D) applies only 'Beginning January 1, 2027, and ending July 31, 2027'

Consumer rights suite (access, correction, deletion, portability, 45-day response, privacy notice, processor contracts) exceeds the fixed duty vocabulary; closest duties assigned above, remainder not separately codable

Known-child provisions exist (sensitive data includes 'Personal data collected from a known child'; COPPA parental-consent safe harbor in §1780.2(E)) but the act is not minors-focused, so minorsFocus not coded
§1780.4(P) separately prohibits entities described by §1780.2(A)(3) from selling sensitive personal data without prior consent
